Tomato___Early_blight.description: A common fungal disease of tomato and potato. It starts on the older, lower leaves and moves up the plant. Badly infected leaves turn brown and fall off.
Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Small dark spots on lower leaves that grow into round brown spots with target-like rings. The area around each spot often turns yellow.
guidance: Remove leaves with spots and bury or burn them. Do not compost them.
Water at the base of the plant and use mulch so soil does not splash onto the leaves.
Stake the plants and leave space between them so the leaves dry faster.
Do not plant tomatoes or peppers in the same spot for two years.

Tomato___Late_blight.description: A fast-spreading disease of tomato and potato that is worst in cool, wet weather. It can destroy plants within days once it takes hold.
Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Irregular, water-soaked patches that turn light brown, often starting on the upper leaves. In humid weather, white fuzzy growth can appear under the leaves.
guidance: Remove and destroy infected plants and fruit straight away to slow the spread.
Avoid wetting the leaves when watering, and water early in the day.
Choose resistant varieties when planting again.
Ask a local agriculture officer before using any fungicide, as treatment works best before infection.

Tomato___healthy.description: No signs of disease were detected on this leaf.
guidance: Keep checking the older, lower leaves, where many diseases start.
Water at the base of the plant and keep the leaves dry.
Leave space between plants so air can flow.
Remove weeds and fallen plant debris around the plants.
